hindi: अब इसलिए हम प्रकृति के भेदों से सम्बन्धित शारीर यानी शरीर सम्बन्धी की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Śārīra (that which relates to the body) concerning the kinds of constitution (prakṛti).
notes: Chapter-opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). Both accusatives are adjectival; the unstated noun (chapter, section) is not supplied, as in p02 ch04 u1. prakṛti here = the natural bodily constitution (the seven types of the next unit), standard; elsewhere in Part 2 it can mean the natural state.

hindi: प्रकृतियाँ सात हैं: दोषों से अलग-अलग, मेल से और समता से।
english: There are seven constitutions (prakṛti): from the doṣas singly, from combination, and from equality.
notes: The seven are, by the later units: Vāta, Pitta, Kapha singly (3), three of two combined, and the equal (sama) one. Printed bhavaṃti = bhavanti (anusvāra for n, orthography). 'sāmyena' = by equality (of the three doṣas), as unit 34 shows.
lines_deva: सप्त प्रकृतयो दोषैः पृथक् संसर्गेण साम्येन च भवंति
lines_iast: sapta prakṛtayo doṣaiḥ pṛthak saṃsargeṇa sāmyena ca bhavaṃti

words.gloss: of a snake (āśīviṣa, lit. one with poison in its fangs)

hindi: वहाँ शुक्र, आर्तव, गर्भाशय और काल में तथा माता के आहार और विहार में, जो एक या अनेक दोष अधिकता से हो, उससे, अनुमानित पाठ पर मृत्यु तक, प्रकृति उत्पन्न होती है, जैसे विष की बेल में उत्पन्न होने वाले कृमि के लिए विष से, विषैले कृमि, बिच्छू आदि के लिए, अथवा सर्प के लिए अपने विष से।
english: There, whichever doṣa, one or more, becomes predominant in the semen (śukra), the menstrual fluid (ārtava), the womb (garbhāśaya) and the time, and in the mother's food and conduct, by that, until death (on a conjectural reading), the constitution (prakṛti) arises, as for a worm being born in a poison-creeper, by the poison; like a poisonous worm, a scorpion and so on, or like a snake, by its own poison.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āhvi' is not a word; visarga/ha for ta or da before v (OCR confusion), and the m-ra-ṇā reading is the plainest

notes: Hard, partly garbled sentence; the sense is that each creature's own poison does not harm it, as the constitution does not harm the person. Printed 'tenāmaraṇāhviṣavalyāmiva' is read tena ā-maraṇāt viṣa-valyām iva; 'āhvi' looks like a damaged 'āt vi' (flagged, possible). 'vṛścikāder' (scorpion and so on) and 'saviṣa-kṛmer' are taken as comparisons; the exact attachment of the genitives is uncertain. Whether 'ā-maraṇāt' goes with 'tena' as 'lifelong' is a reading, not firm. śukra = semen, ārtava = menstrual fluid, garbhāśaya = womb (all standard). Printed 'ekoneko' avagraha: eko 'nekaḥ.

words.gloss: that; being made of, consisting of

hindi: इसलिए उसी से बने होने के कारण, शरीर के शुक्र और आर्तव से भावित यानी भीगे हुए होने के कारण और प्राकृत होने के कारण वह उस दोष से उतने में आहत नहीं होता।
english: Therefore, because of being made of that, because the body is soaked (bhāvita) by the semen (śukra) and the menstrual fluid (ārtava), and because of being natural (prākṛta), it is not harmed to that extent by that doṣa.
notes: The genitive in 'śukrārtavayor dehasya bhāvitatvāt' is taken as 'the body's being soaked by the two'; the alternative 'the body of semen and ārtava being soaked' gives the same sense. 'it' (the person or body) is not stated; the subject of vihanyate is understood. tanmayatā = the state of being made of that (the doṣa of unit 3).
lines_deva: तस्मान्तन्मयतया शुक्रार्तवयोर्देहस्य भावितत्वात्प्राकृतत्वाच्च तावता तेन दोषेण न विहन्यते
lines_iast: tasmāntanmayatayā śukrārtavayordehasya bhāvitatvātprākṛtatvācca tāvatā tena doṣeṇa na vihanyate

hindi: और इसका शरीर उसी के गुणों से ही गढ़ा जाता है। और इसलिए वह उसके गुणों के विरोधियों से अचानक पीड़ित नहीं होता।
english: And his body is furnished (upaskriyate) by the qualities of that (doṣa) alone. And therefore he is not suddenly afflicted by the opposites of its qualities.
notes: [02.08.5] 'tad' refers to the doṣa of unit 3. upaskriyate = equipped, formed, built up. [02.08.6] The subject 'he' (the person, or the body) is understood. 'tad-guṇa' refers to the qualities of the doṣa that forms the constitution.

hindi: किन्तु उस अवस्था में, जब दोष विकृति वाला और उल्बण यानी बढ़ा हुआ हो, गर्भ बनता ही नहीं।
english: But in that state, when the doṣa is abnormal (vikṛtimat) and excessive (ulbaṇa), the embryo (garbha) does not come into being at all.
notes: Locative absolute. Printed 'doṣeulbaṇe' joins doṣe + ulbaṇe without sandhi (print habit, no flag). vikṛti = abnormality (glossary).
lines_deva: तस्यां त्ववस्थायां विकृतिमति दोषेउल्बणे नैव गर्भः संभवति
lines_iast: tasyāṃ tvavasthāyāṃ vikṛtimati doṣeulbaṇe naiva garbhaḥ saṃbhavati

hindi: गर्भ बनते ही नष्ट हो जाता है, अथवा विकृत हो जाता है।
english: Even at conception it perishes (vipadyate), or it becomes abnormal (vikṛta).
notes: Printed 'saṃbhavaeva' is read saṃbhave eva (e before a vowel written as a, hiatus kept); it could also be read saṃbhava eva, 'conception itself', with the same sense. The subject 'it' (the embryo) is carried from unit 7. vikṛta may also mean deformed.

hindi: और इसी प्रकार कुछ लोग कहते हैं।
english: And so some say.
notes: Introduces a view; the statement continues in the next units. 'kecit' is a masculine plural pronoun here ('some').

hindi: वात आदि दो प्रकार के हैं: प्राकृत और वैकृत।
english: Vāta and the others are of two kinds: natural (prākṛta) and abnormal (vaikṛta).
notes: 'Vāta and the others' = Vāta, Pitta, Kapha. Final visarga lost before v- is regular sandhi (prākṛtā vaikṛtāḥ), no flag. Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें प्राकृत सात प्रकार की प्रकृति के कारण हैं और शरीर के साथ ही एक साथ जन्मे हैं।
english: Among these, the natural (prākṛta) ones are the causes of the sevenfold constitution (prakṛti), having one birth with the body.
notes: 'The natural ones' are the natural Vāta, Pitta and Kapha of unit 10. 'Having one birth with the body' = born together with the body. Copula understood.

hindi: वे शरीर को धारण करने के कारण धातु नाम वाले हैं; अस्पष्ट पद दोषार्व्यानां वाले विकृतों के, बीज बने हुओं के, मरने की इच्छा वाले यानी मरणासन्न के, वे अपने स्वरूप से हट जाते हैं।
english: They have the name dhātu from supporting the body; of the unclear (doṣārvyānām) abnormal (vikṛta) ones, being the seed (bīja), in one about to die they move away from their own nature (svarūpa).

text_flags.why: possible: 'rvya' does not form a word; the context (vikṛtānām bījabhūtānām) suggests a word about doṣas, but the reading is not sure

notes: Damaged: 'doṣārvyānāṃ' does not parse and is left unsplit and unclear. The syntax of the genitives (vikṛtānām bījabhūtānām, mumūrṣoḥ) is uncertain, so the second half is a literal, loose rendering and should not be relied on. 'dhātu' here is explained by the text itself as from 'supporting the body' (dhāraṇa); dhātu is kept as a doctrinal term. 'mumūrṣu' = one wishing to die, i.e. dying.
lines_deva: ते शरीरधारणाद्धातुसंज्ञाः दोषार्व्यानां विकृतानां बीजभूतानां मुमूर्षोः स्वरूपाच्चलंति

hindi: शरीर में सबके उपस्थित होने पर भी प्रकृति में उल्बण यानी बढ़े हुए के द्वारा नामकरण होता है।
english: Even when all are present in the body, in the matter of constitution (prakṛti) the designation is by the prominent (ulbaṇa) one.
notes: 'All' = the three doṣas. Locative absolute (sarveṣu sannihiteṣu). 'ulbaṇena' stands for an unstated noun, shown as 'one'. Copula understood.

hindi: परन्तु वैकृत, गर्भ से बाहर आए हुए के आहारों से, अस्पष्ट पद असात्, उत्पन्न होते हुए, प्राकृतों पर ही जमते हैं; वे काल आदि के प्रभाव से अस्पष्ट पद स्वप्नमाणवृद्धिक्षययोगात् के कारण शरीर को अनुगृहीत करते हैं और दूषित भी करते हैं। उसी प्रकार ओज भी परम, हृदय में स्थित, आठ बूँद के माप का आधार है; अस्पष्ट पद प्राकृतिकल्य; रस स्वरूप वाले, क्षय और वृद्धि में भागी ओज का।
english: But the abnormal (vaikṛta) ones, arising from the foods of one who has come out of the womb, [unclear: asāt], grow only upon the natural (prākṛta) ones; by the force of time and so on, through [unclear: svapnamāṇavṛddhikṣayayogāt], they favour the body and also vitiate it. Likewise ojas too, supreme, situated in the heart, of the measure of eight drops, is the support; [unclear: prākṛtikalya]; of ojas, whose nature is rasa, sharing in decrease and increase.

possible: 'svapnamāṇa' does not make sense beside vṛddhi-kṣaya; svamāna or svapramāṇa fits better
possible: the word does not parse as printed; the correction is a guess

notes: Heavily damaged and run-together. Left unsplit and unclear: 'asāt' (maybe asātmyāt, 'unsuitable'), 'svapnamāṇavṛddhikṣayayogāt' (perhaps a lost svamāna/svapramāṇa: 'by connection with decrease and increase of its own measure', not adopted) and 'prākṛtikalya'. The last four clauses on ojas are a loose literal rendering: 'ādhāraḥ' (support) has no stated object, and the two genitives rasātmakasya ojasaḥ with kṣayavṛddhibhājaḥ are taken as one phrase 'of ojas, which is of the nature of rasa and shares in decrease and increase'. 'ojas' is kept as a doctrinal term (the vital essence residing in the heart; the text gives only its position and measure: eight drops). 'aṣṭabindu' = eight drops.
lines_deva: वैकृतास्तु गर्भादभिनिःसृतस्याहारैरसात्संभवंतः प्राकृतेष्वेव रोहंति ते कालादिवशेन स्वप्नमाणवृद्धिक्षययोगाद्देहमनुगृह्णंति दूषयंति च तद्वदोजोऽपि परं हृदयस्थमष्टबिंदुप्रमाणमाधारः प्राकृतिकल्य रसात्मकस्यौजसः क्षयवृद्धिभाजः

hindi: अब अपने दोष के गुणों के अनुसार वात प्रकृति वाला दुबला और रूखा होता है; उसके अंग, दाँत, नाखून, रोम, नेत्र और स्वर पतले और कम होते हैं; वह शीत से द्वेष करने वाला है, पिंडलियाँ कसी हुई हैं; सशब्द जोड़ों से चलता है; आरम्भ, क्षोभ, ग्रहण और भूलने में शीघ्र है; धैर्य, बुद्धि, चाल, दृष्टि, स्वभाव और मित्रता में चंचल है; चोर है, अनार्य है; ईर्ष्यालु है, इन्द्रियों को न जीतने वाला है; गान्धर्व यानी संगीत, इतिहास, हास, विलास, कलह, शिकार, उद्यान और यात्रा का प्रिय है; और चिकने, गरम, मीठे, अनुमानित पाठ पर खट्टे, नमकीन अन्न और पान की इच्छा तथा अनुकूलता वाला होता है।
english: Now, in accordance with the qualities of his own doṣa, one of Vāta constitution (vātaprakṛti) is thin and dry, with thin and scanty limbs, teeth, nails, hair, eyes and voice; a hater of cold, with tightly bound (udbaddha) calves; going with noisy joints; quick to begin, to be agitated, to grasp and to forget; unsteady in fortitude, mind, gait, gaze, disposition and friendship; a thief, ignoble; envious, with his senses unconquered; fond of music (gāndharva), legends (itihāsa), laughter, play, quarrel, hunting, gardens and journeys; and with a desire for, and suitability to, unctuous, hot, sweet, sour (on a conjectural reading) and salty food and drink.

notes: Long list of marks; the verb 'bhavati' ends it. Printed 'śītadvidudvaddha' is read śīta-dviṭ + udbaddha (d before a vowel by sandhi; v for b is the print's v/b interchange, recorded once): 'hater of cold' is a reading, not firm. 'tanū-rūkṣaḥ' is regular sandhi of tanuḥ rūkṣaḥ. 'tanu-alpa' is taken to qualify all six items (limbs, teeth, nails, hair, eyes, voice). 'matsaryajitendriyaḥ' = matsarī + ajita-indriyaḥ by sandhi (envious, senses not conquered); the alternative 'jita' (conquered) does not fit the list of faults. 'gāndharva' = music, song (probable); 'itihāsa' = legend, tales. 'dhṛti' here = fortitude, steadiness. 'upaśaya' = what suits; 'kāṅkṣā-upaśaya' read as desire and suitability. 'stena' = thief, a noun in the list (so 'a thief'), not 'inclined to steal'. Printed 'madhurāmsa' is a slip for madhura-amla (flagged).

hindi: थोड़े धन, बल, जीवन और नींद वाला; कृश वाणी वाला, धमनी यानी सम्भवतः दिखाई देने वाली नसों से फैले हुए गात्र वाला। दुर्भाग्य वाला, बहुत खाने वाला, बहुत बोलने वाला, नास्तिक, फटे हुए केश, हाथ और पैर वाला।
english: With little wealth, strength, life and sleep; with weak (kṣāma) speech and a body spread over with vessels (dhamanī, probably the visible veins). Unfortunate, eating very much, talkative, an unbeliever (nāstika), with split hair, hands and feet.
notes: [02.08.17] Continues the Vāta description (the verb 'bhavati' of unit 15 is not repeated). kṣāma is taken with vāc (weak or hoarse speech) in the glossary sense 'kṛśa'; it might instead qualify the whole man ('emaciated; speech ...'), so the split of the compound is not firm. dhamanī (vessel; here probably the visible veins) is probable, not stated. The short -i of 'dhamani-' in the compound is metrical or print. [02.08.18] 'durbhaga' = unlucky or unfortunate (the sense of disagreeable to others is also possible). 'sphuṭita' = split, cracked; whether it applies equally to hair is not stated (taken as one compound, as printed). 'nāstika' = one who denies (the next world, or the Veda).

hindi: थोड़ी खुली दृष्टि और बहुत ढीले मुख वाला; वह कराहता है, अस्पष्ट पद क्थति, दाँतों को चबाता है। वह सूखी, रूखी और ऊबड़-खाबड़ नदियों में, आकाश में और पर्वत की चोटियों पर जाता है।
english: With eyes slightly open and the mouth very slack (susrasta); he moans (stanyate), [unclear: kthati], and grinds his teeth. He goes in dry, rough and uneven rivers, in the sky and on mountain peaks.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kthati' does not parse; a verb of noise such as kūthati (groans) fits beside stanyate and khādati dantān, but this is a guess

notes: [02.08.19] Hard and partly damaged; confidence low. The compound is split as kiñcit-unmiṣita-dṛk-mukha-su-srastaḥ, 'eye slightly opened, mouth very slack'; the join of mukha with what precedes or follows is not sure. 'kthati' is not a known word and is left unclear (kūthati, 'groans', is a guess, flagged only). 'susrastastanyate' is read susrastaḥ stanyate (visarga before st); 'stanyate' for a middle form of √stan is irregular, so the form is not sure. No word for sleep or dream is in this unit (context of units 20 and 26 suggests it), so none is supplied. [02.08.20] The subject 'he' (the Vāta person) is understood. No word for dream is in the unit, so none is supplied (cf. unit 26 'suptaḥ' and unit 32 'svapne').

karabha (camel or young elephant); tawny; sparse; soft; head hair; body hair

sweet; bitter; astringent; cold; desire; suitability

hindi: पित्त प्रकृति वाला गरम और गोरे शरीर वाला होता है; उसके नाखून, नेत्र, जीभ, होंठ, हथेलियाँ और तलवे ताँबे के रंग के होते हैं; जोड़ों के बन्धन और मांस ढीले होते हैं; केश और रोम करभ यानी ऊँट या हाथी के बच्चे के समान कपिल यानी भूरे, विरल और मुलायम होते हैं; बल और आयु मध्यम होती है, शुक्र, मैथुन और सन्तान थोड़ी होती है; शूर है, अभिमानी है; झुर्रियाँ, गंजापन, बाल पकना, फुंसियाँ और झाइयाँ जल्दी होती हैं, अनुमानित पाठ पर उसे भूख और प्यास लगती है; मेधावी है, दुर्भाग्य वाला है; और मीठे, कड़वे, कसैले और ठंडे की इच्छा तथा अनुकूलता वाला होता है।
english: One of Pitta constitution (pittaprakṛti) is warm and fair-bodied, with copper-coloured nails, eyes, tongue, lips, palms and soles; with loose joint-ligaments and flesh; with hair of the head and body like a karabha (camel or young elephant), tawny, sparse and soft; of middling strength and life, with little semen, sexual intercourse and offspring; brave, proud; with early wrinkles (valī), baldness (khalita), grey hair (palita), pimples (piṭka) and blemishes (vyaṅga) and, on a conjectural reading, hunger and thirst; intelligent, unfortunate; and with desire for, and suitability to, sweet, bitter, astringent (kaṣāya) and cold (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sṛt' is not a word beside pipāsa; kṣut (hunger) fits, as in unit 27 (kṣutpipāsā); also 'piṭku' for piṭka/piṭaka (short u for a, OCR)

notes: Printed 'sṛtpipāso' is read kṣut-pipāsaḥ (hunger and thirst, as in unit 27 kṣutpipāsā): the translation adopts this and is marked conjectural; flagged. 'karabha-kapila' is read as 'tawny like a karabha'; karabha = camel (or young elephant), so the comparison is not firm. 'śīghra' is taken to qualify the whole list of skin and hair changes ('early'). 'alpa-śukra-vyavāya-apatya' = little semen, intercourse and offspring. The taste list is a dvandva; kaṣāya here is the taste (astringent). 'upaśaya' = what suits. Copula 'bhavati' ends the unit. śukra = semen (standard).
lines_deva: पित्तप्रकृतिरुष्णगौरगात्रस्ताम्रनखनयनजिह्वौष्ठपाणिपादतलः शिथिलसंधिबंधमांसः करभकपिलविरलमृदुकेशरोमा मध्यबलायुरल्पशुक्रव्यवायापत्यः शूरोऽभिमानी शीघ्रवलीखलितपलितपिट्कुव्यंगसृत्पिपासो मेधावी दुर्भगः स्वादुतित्तकषायशीताभिलाषोपशयश्च भवति

words.gloss: wealth, power; daring; intellect; strength; endowed with

hindi: माला, लेप और सजावट जिसे प्रिय हैं; सदाचारी, शुद्ध, आश्रितों पर स्नेह करने वाला। वैभव, साहस, बुद्धि और बल से युक्त होता है; भय में दिशाओं के स्वामियों के लिए भी वह आश्रय होता है।
english: One to whom garlands, unguents and adornment are dear; well-behaved, pure, affectionate to his dependents. He is endowed with wealth (vibhava), daring, intellect and strength; in fears he is a refuge even for the lords of the quarters (dikpati).
notes: [02.08.23] Continues the Pitta description (verb of unit 21 not repeated). 'dayita' may be taken with all three nouns (as printed, one compound). śuci = pure or clean (both senses possible). [02.08.24] Printed 'valānvito' has v for b (print habit, normalised once to bala); 'diṃpatām' = dik-patām (ṃ for ṅ, orthography). 'bhīṣu' is the locative plural of bhī (fear); 'gatiḥ' = refuge or resort; 'for the lords of the quarters' (genitive) could also be 'of' them in the sense of belonging, so the exact relation is not firm. vibhava = wealth or power.

words.gloss: much; stool; anger; drinking; eating; jealousy
quarters; burning; meteor; lightning; sun; fire

hindi: गरमी से द्वेष करने वाला, पसीने वाला, अनुमानित पाठ पर दुर्गन्ध वाला, जिसे मल, क्रोध, पान, भोजन और ईर्ष्या बहुत होते हैं। सोया हुआ वह कर्णिकार यानी सम्भवतः कनकचम्पा के वृक्ष, पलाश यानी ढाक के वृक्ष, दिशाओं का जलना, उल्का, बिजली, सूर्य और अग्नि देखे।
english: A hater of heat, sweating, foul-smelling (on a conjectural reading), with much stool, anger, drinking, eating and jealousy. Asleep, he would see karṇikāra trees (probably the kanak-champa tree), palāśa trees (the dhak or flame-of-the-forest), the burning of the quarters (digdāha), meteors, lightning, the sun and fires.

text_flags.why: possible: 'pūniṃ' is not a word before gandhi; pūti (foul) fits the list of faults, a guess from sense

notes: [02.08.25] Printed 'pūniṃgaṃdhir' is read pūti-gandhiḥ (flagged, possible). 'bhūri' is taken to qualify the whole list as printed. 'svedana' = sweating (the plain sense; 'causing sweat' is possible). 'uccāra' = stool, excretion. Verb of unit 21 not repeated. [02.08.26] Identifications: karṇikāra = Pterospermum acerifolium (probable; Cassia fistula is another proposal), palāśa = Butea monosperma (standard). 'digdāha' = burning of the quarters (a glow or fire seen in the horizon). 'arka' is taken as the sun (it can also be Calotropis); 'suptaḥ' with the opt. 'paśyet' is read as seeing in sleep, i.e. dreaming. The first token is run together: suptaḥ paśyet karṇikārān.

dūrvā (Cynodon dactylon grass; standard); indīvara (blue lotus, Nymphaea; probable); śara reed (Saccharum, probable); stalk; any one of; colour
even; well; divided, proportioned; unctuous; firm; delicate; smooth
full, well developed; handsome; limbs, body
distinct; white; dark; clear; long; wide; lashes, having; eyes
much; ojas; strength; semen; intercourse; offspring
pungent; bitter; astringent; hot; dry; desire; suitability

hindi: कफ प्रकृति वाला दूर्वा यानी दूब, इन्दीवर यानी सम्भवतः नीले कमल, या शर यानी सम्भवतः सरकंडे के डंठल में से किसी एक के रंग का होता है; वह सम, अनुमानित पाठ पर सुविभक्त, स्निग्ध, स्थिर, सुकुमार और मसृण है, अनुमानित पाठ पर उसके जोड़ों के बन्धन अच्छे हैं; वह भरे हुए सुन्दर शरीर वाला है; उसका ललाट, जाँघें और भुजाएँ बड़ी हैं; आँखों में सफेद और काला साफ दिखता है, वे स्वच्छ, लम्बी, चौड़ी और पलकों वाली हैं; उसकी ध्वनि सिंह, मृदंग और मेघ जैसी है; वह भूख, प्यास और गरमी सह लेता है; उसके ओज, बल, शुक्र, मैथुन और सन्तान अनुमानित पाठ पर बहुत हैं; अस्पष्ट पद स्थिरशोष, माला और लेप वाला है; उसकी शत्रुता दृढ़ और छिपी हुई है; वह सुकोमल, सत्यवादी, स्मृति वाला, धैर्य वाला, लोभ रहित है; बचपन में भी रोता नहीं; और कटु यानी तीखे, कड़वे, कसैले, गरम और रूखे की इच्छा तथा अनुकूलता वाला होता है।
english: But one of Kapha constitution (kaphaprakṛti) has the colour of any one of dūrvā grass (Bermuda grass), indīvara (probably the blue lotus) or the stalk of the śara reed (probably a reed grass); even, well-proportioned (on a conjectural reading), unctuous, firm, delicate, smooth, with joint-ligaments well-fitted (on a conjectural reading); with a full, handsome body; with a large forehead, thighs and arms; with eyes in which the white and the dark are distinct, clear, long, wide and lashed; with a sound like a lion, a mṛdaṅga drum and a cloud; enduring hunger, thirst and heat; with much (on a conjectural reading) ojas, strength, semen, sexual intercourse and offspring; [unclear: sthiraśoṣa], garlands and unguents; with firm, hidden enmity; gentle, truthful; possessing memory and steadiness, not greedy, not crying even in childhood; and with desire for, and suitability to, pungent (kaṭu), bitter, astringent (kaṣāya), hot and dry (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: 'mu' for su and 'sasa' for susa (OCR); sama and su-sandhi-bandha are the sense
possible: 'banhojo' for bahvojo (h/n confusion); 'sthiraśoṣa' unclear (śobhā or śoka are guesses)

notes: Several prints need care. 'samamuvibhakta' is read sama-su-vibhakta and 'sasaṃdhibaṃdhaḥ' as su-sandhi-bandhaḥ (flagged, possible). 'banhojo' is read bahu-ojaḥ (a conjectural reading, flagged: it matches Pitta's alpa-śukra-vyavāya-apatya in unit 21); the translation marks it. 'sthiraśoṣa' is damaged or unknown (śoṣa = drying up does not suit) and is left unsplit and unclear. 'mahā' is taken with the whole trio (forehead, thighs, arms); 'uru' could instead mean broad (broad arms). 'ghana' = cloud (or deep, dense). 'peśala' = gentle, charming (skilful is possible). Identifications: dūrvā = Cynodon dactylon (standard); indīvara = a blue water-lily or lotus, Nymphaea (probable); śara = a reed of the Saccharum group (probable). kaṭu = pungent; kaṣāya here = the taste, astringent. Printed 'bālyepyarodanaḥ' = bālye api arodanaḥ.
lines_deva: कफप्रकृतिस्तु दूर्वेदीवरशरकांडान्यतमवर्णः सममुविभक्तस्निग्धस्थिरसुकुमारश्लक्ष्णःससंधिबंधः परिपूर्णचारुगात्रो महाललाटोरुबाहुर्व्यक्तसितासितप्रसन्नायतनविशालपक्ष्मलाक्षः सिंहमृदंगघनघोषः क्षुत्पिपासोष्णसहिष्णुर्बन्होजोबलशुक्रव्यवायापत्यस्थिरशोषमाल्यानुलेपनो दृढप्रच्छन्नवैरः पेशलः सत्यवादी स्मृतिमान्धृतिमानलोलुपो बाल्येप्यरोदनः कटुतित्तकषायोष्णरूक्षेच्छोपशयश्च भवति

words.gloss: little; speech; anger; intellect; eating; effort, desire

hindi: थोड़ी वाणी, क्रोध, मेधा, भोजन और चेष्टा वाला; बहुत आयु और धन वाला; दूरदर्शी, उदार। श्रद्धालु, गम्भीर, स्थूललक्ष यानी बड़े लक्ष्य वाला, क्षमावान, श्रेष्ठ, निद्रालु यानी सोने की प्रवृत्ति वाला, दीर्घसूत्री यानी देर लगाने वाला, कृतज्ञ।
english: With little speech, anger, intellect (medhā), eating and effort; with abundant life and wealth; far-seeing, generous. Faithful (śrāddha), deep, of large aim (sthūlalakṣa), forbearing, noble, prone to sleep, slow-acting (dīrghasūtrī), grateful.
notes: [02.08.29] Continues the Kapha description (verb of unit 27 not repeated). The compound alpa-vyāhāra-krodha-medhā-aśana-īha is read as printed, with 'alpa' qualifying all five; 'medhā' (intellect) is odd in a list of Kapha's small things (meha is conceivable) and 'īha' may be effort or desire, so this compound is not firm. 'dīrgha-darśī' = far-sighted. [02.08.30] 'śrāddha' = faithful, trusting (it can also relate to the ancestral rite, not here). 'sthūlalakṣa' is taken literally as 'of large aim'; some commentators take it as 'noticing big things / liberal', so the sense is not firm. 'dīrghasūtrī' = lit. 'long-threaded', idiomatically slow to act. Verb of unit 27 not repeated.
lines_deva: श्राद्धो गंभीरः स्थूललक्षः क्षमावानार्यो निद्रालुर्दीर्घसूत्री कृतज्ञः
lines_iast: śrāddho gaṃbhīraḥ sthūlalakṣaḥ kṣamāvānāryo nidrālurdīrghasūtrī kṛtajñaḥ

hindi: सीधा, विद्वान, सौभाग्यशाली, लज्जावान, गुरुओं का भक्त, दृढ़ मित्रता वाला। स्वप्न में वह कमलों वाले और पक्षियों की पंक्तियों वाले जलाशयों को और बादलों को देखता है।
english: Upright, learned, fortunate, modest, devoted to his elders (guru), of firm friendship. In a dream he sees water-reservoirs (toyāśaya) with lotuses (padma) and with rows of birds, and clouds (toyada, giver of water).
notes: [02.08.31] Continues the Kapha description. guru here = elder or teacher (a plural of respect). [02.08.32] Identification: padma = lotus (Nelumbo nucifera; standard). toyāśaya = pond, lake or any water-receptacle; 'sa-padma' and 'sa-vihaṅgamāla' are taken with it. toyada = cloud (lit. water-giving).

hindi: किन्तु दोनों के लक्षणों के मिलने पर संसर्ग से बनी होती है। सब गुणों से युक्त समदोष प्रकृति वाला होता है।
english: But when the marks of both are mixed, [it is] the one made by combination (saṃsarga). One endowed with all the qualities is of the equal-doṣa constitution (samadoṣaprakṛti).
notes: [02.08.33] Copula understood. 'saṃsarga-kṛti' is taken as 'made by combination', i.e. the combined (dual) constitution of unit 2; the noun it describes (prakṛti) is not stated, so the bracketed 'it' is only the understood subject. 'Both' = two of the three doṣas. [02.08.34] Copula understood. 'All the qualities' is read as the marks of all three doṣas together (not necessarily 'all good qualities'); samadoṣa = the three doṣas in balance (the seventh constitution of unit 2).

hindi: उनमें पहले तीन सदा रोगी रहने वाले हैं, अस्पष्ट पद दोषानुप्रशयितप्रकृतित्वात् के कारण।
english: Among these, the first three are always ailing (nitya-ātura), because of [unclear: doṣānupraśayitaprakṛtitvāt].

text_flags.why: possible: 'anupraśayita' is not a known form; anuśayita (clinging, attached) fits, but this is a guess

notes: The last word is damaged or unknown ('anupraśayita' is not a recognised form) and is left unsplit and unclear. A plausible sense is 'because their constitution is attached to (lies along) the doṣa' (doṣa-anuśayita-prakṛti-tva), but this is a guess and is not used in the translation. 'The first three' = the three single-doṣa constitutions; the noun 'constitutions' is not stated, and the gram is given for the adjective only. Reviewer: ādyāḥ trayaḥ nityāturāḥ are masculine plural, so the unstated noun is masculine (persons of those types), not the feminine prakṛtayaḥ.

hindi: और विशेष रूप से द्वन्द्व प्रकृति वाले।
english: And especially those of dual constitution (dvandvaprakṛti).
notes: Elliptical: the predicate 'always ailing' is carried from unit 35 and is not supplied. 'Those' shows the unstated noun. 'dvandva' = the pair of doṣas combined.

hindi: क्योंकि उनमें, जो गुणों के मिश्रण से विकार करने वाले हैं, भूख, प्यास आदि में, अनुमानित पाठ पर अनारोग्य का नामकरण होता है।
english: For in these, which produce disorders of mixed qualities, in hunger, thirst and so on, there is, on a conjectural reading, the designation of ill-health (anārogya).

text_flags.why: possible: 'avārogya' is not a known word; an-ārogya (ill-health) fits the sense; the correction is a guess from sense

notes: Printed 'avārogya' is read an-ārogya (n/v confusion in this print); the translation adopts this and is marked conjectural. The two locatives 'teṣu ... kāriṣu' and 'kṣutpipāsādiṣu' are taken together; the exact grammar (whether hunger and thirst are what produces the disorders) is not sure. Copula understood. 'vikāra' = disorder.

words.gloss: doṣa; treatment (upakramaṇīya; probably a chapter title); stated

hindi: इसलिए उनका उपचार विपरीत गुणों वाली उस विधि से करना चाहिए जो दोषोपक्रमणीय में कही गई है।
english: Therefore one should treat them with a method of opposite qualities, as stated in the Doṣopakramaṇīya (the treatment of the doṣas).
notes: The antecedent of 'tān' (them) is not in this unit; it is read as the constitutions (prakṛti) of the preceding units. 'doṣopakramaṇīya' is probably the title of an earlier chapter on the treatment of the doṣas (probable); read as a locative-sense 'stated in the ...'. upācaret is 'one should treat / apply treatment to'.

words.gloss: with what is suited (sātmya: suited by habit)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: सम को सभी रसों से और सात्म्य यानी अनुकूल से, और दूसरों को ऋतु के अनुसार विहित से भी। अनुमानित पाठ पर: दोषों के समान ही, सत्त्व आदि गुणों से भी सात प्रकृतियाँ होती हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading: the balanced (one) with all tastes (rasa) and with what is suited (sātmya); and the others also with what is prescribed according to the season. On a conjectural reading: like the doṣas, and also by the qualities beginning with sattva, there are seven constitutions (prakṛti).

text_flags.why: possible: 'semaṃ' is not a word; 'samam' (balanced, as in samadoṣaprakṛti of unit 34 and sama prakṛti of 40/42) fits; e/a confusion

possible but well supported: 'sama' leaves 'prakṛtayaḥ' without a number; unit 42 lists seven bases (jāti, kula, deśa, kāla, vaya, bala, pratyātma) and unit 43 has 'saptādīnām'; pta/ma is a known OCR confusion in this scan

notes: [02.08.39] Elliptical: the verb is carried from 38 (upācaret, 'one should treat'); the translation supplies none. The printed 'semaṃ' is read as 'samam' on a conjectural reading; 'samam' could also be the adverb 'equally'. 'sarva-rasena' is read as 'with all tastes' (a regimen of all six tastes is not stated; only the instrumental is given); the thing applied is not named, so no noun is added. 'anyāṃś ca' (and the others) taken with 'yathartuvihitena' ('prescribed according to the season'); the first ca joins 'others', the second joins the two halves. Reading and syntax are uncertain. [02.08.40] Read as 'sapta prakṛtayaḥ' on a conjectural reading (see text_flag); the alternative 'samāḥ prakṛtayaḥ' would give 'the constitutions are balanced', which fits neither the context (units 31-37 list single, dual and balanced constitutions) nor 43. prakṛti kept as 'constitution' (the doctrinal term). 'doṣavat' = 'like the doṣas' (suffix -vat); read as 'as with the doṣas, so with the guṇas'. sattva = mind (standard).
lines_deva: दोषवच्च गुणैरपि सत्त्वादिभिः सम प्रकृतयो भवंति
lines_iast: doṣavacca guṇairapi sattvādibhiḥ sama prakṛtayo bhavaṃti

hindi: उन्हें केवल उन्हीं से उत्पन्न, जैसा कहा गया है, शौच आदि से जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know them by cleanliness (śauca) and the like, as stated, arisen only from them.
notes: Several lines in the chunk start 'tāḥ' = the constitutions (prakṛti, f. pl.) of 40, antecedent assumed. 'tad-abhinivṛtta' = produced from it/them, an adjective agreeing with śaucādibhiḥ ('cleanliness etc. produced from them'). Sandhi: tāḥ+tad > tās tad; abhinivṛttair+eva; śaucādibhir+jānīyāt (regular).

words.gloss: birth-class (jāti); family; region; time; age; strength; each individual; basis, support

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: उसी प्रकार फिर सात प्रकृतियाँ जाति, कुल, देश, काल, वय, बल और प्रत्येक व्यक्ति पर आश्रित हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading: likewise, again, the seven constitutions (prakṛti) are based on birth-class (jāti), family, region, time, age, strength, and each individual.

text_flags.why: possible but well supported: seven bases are listed in this very unit; 'saptādīnām' in 43; pta/ma OCR confusion (see unit 40)

notes: Copula understood (verbless unit); 'are' supplied in the translation. 'saṃśraya' = basis, resting on; 'pratyātma' = in each self / each individual. 'jāti' could be caste, species or birth-class; 'birth-class' used. prakṛtayaḥ+jāti is regular sandhi (prakṛtayo jāti). Seven items in the compound match 'sapta'.

words.gloss: birth-class (jāti); and so on; fixed, determined
other; conformity, following; the state of

hindi: क्योंकि पुरुषों में जाति आदि से निश्चित वे-वे भाव-विशेष दिखाई देते हैं; और सात आदि के कम-अधिक योग से, शरीर की विशेषताओं से और दूसरे के अनुसरण के कारण भेदों का कुल विस्तार अगणित हो जाता है।
english: For among men are seen those various particular states (bhāva) determined by birth-class (jāti) and the rest; and by the more-and-most degrees of combination of the seven and others, by differences of body, and because of conformity to another, the total extent of the varieties becomes countless.
notes: Printed spacing 'puruṣāṇāṃjātyādi' (no space) is only a spacing habit. 'te te' = 'those several / each of those'. 'saptādīnām' = of the seven and the rest (the seven constitutions of 42 and, probably, the combinations); 'taratama-yoga' = combination by degrees of more and most. 'anyānuvidhānatva' = 'the state of conforming to another' (see 44: body and sattva conform to each other). 'bhedāgram' = 'bheda-agram', taken as 'the total/extent of varieties' (agra read as extent); this word is the least sure. The long ablative series gives reasons for 'countless'.
lines_deva: दृश्यंते हि पुरुषाणांजात्यादिनियतास्ते ते भावविशेषाः सप्तादीनां च तरतमयोगाच्छरीरविशेषेभ्यश्चान्यानुविधानत्वाच्च भेदाग्रमसंख्येयं भवति
lines_iast: dṛśyaṃte hi puruṣāṇāṃjātyādiniyatāste te bhāvaviśeṣāḥ saptādīnāṃ ca taratamayogāccharīraviśeṣebhyaścānyānuvidhānatvācca bhedāgramasaṃkhyeyaṃ bhavati

words.gram: 3 sg. pres. pass./mid. √dhā (anu-vi), used with acc.

words.gloss: sattva; and so on; countless; varieties; power, influence

hindi: शरीर भी सत्त्व यानी मन आदि का अनुसरण करता है और सत्त्व आदि भी शरीर का; और अनुमानित पाठ पर, सत्त्व आदि के अगणित भेदों के प्रभाव से रूप, स्वर और आचरण की नकल भी, जो अनेक शब्दों से कही जाती है, अगणित भेदों वाली हो जाती है।
english: The body also conforms to sattva (mind) and the rest, and sattva and the rest also conform to the body; and, on a conjectural reading, by the influence of the countless varieties of sattva and the rest, the imitation of form, voice and conduct as well, which is expressible by many words, becomes of countless varieties.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sattvāya-' is not a word; 'sattvādi-' / 'sattvādy-' (as in the two earlier phrases of this unit) with 'asaṃkhyeya' gives the sense; d dropped

notes: 'anuvidhīyate' is passive in form but takes the accusative (sattvādīn) and is read as 'conforms to'; the second clause has the object 'śarīram' for 'sattvādayaḥ' with the same verb understood. The emendation 'sattvādy-asaṃkhyeya-' (flagged) is conjectural; the word 'sattvāya' is otherwise unclear. 'aneka-śabda-vācya' = 'expressible by many words'. Spacing 'bhedaṃbhavati' is a printed joining only.

words.gloss: immediately preceding; birth; practice; latent impression (vāsanā)

words.gram: part of f. inst. sg. vāsanayā

words.gloss: human; animal; departed spirit (preta); inhabitant of hell (nāraka)
anūka (meaning uncertain; possibly lineage or inherited trait)

hindi: परन्तु उसमें प्रवेश तुरन्त पिछले जन्म के अभ्यास के संस्कार से उत्पन्न होता है। इसीलिए मनुष्य, तिर्यक् यानी पशु-पक्षी, प्रेत और नारकी जीवों के, और उनके उन-उन विशेष भेदों के भी, पुरुष के अनूक को, जिसका अर्थ निश्चित नहीं है, यथोचित रूप से ही देखना चाहिए।
english: But the entry into that (tad-āveśa) is produced by the latent impression (vāsanā) of practice in the immediately preceding birth. For that very reason one should examine, accordingly, the anūka (meaning uncertain) of the person, of humans, animals (tiryak), departed spirits (preta) and hell-beings (nāraka), and of their various particular kinds.

text_flags.why: spacing error: a space was printed inside the word vāsanayā (instrumental of vāsanā)

notes: The printed space inside 'vāsa nayā' is a spacing error; the restored word 'vāsanayā' is given under the first token and 'nayā' marks its second half. 'tasmād eva mānuṣa-...' is read 'tasmāt eva' + 'mānuṣa' (the printed 'tasmādevamānuṣa' could also be 'tasmād evaṃ ānuṣa-', but 'ānuṣa' is no word). 'anūka' is uncertain: dictionaries give 'lineage, family' and 'backbone'; read tentatively as an inherited/lineal trait, and left as 'anūka' in the translations; 'puruṣasya' (of the person) and the genitive list of beings are joined loosely. 'tad-āveśa' read as 'the entering into that (state)'. Tiryak = animals (standard); preta = departed spirit; nāraka = being in hell. The sense of the whole unit is not firm.
lines_deva: तदावेशस्त्वनंतरजन्माभ्यासवास नया जन्यते तस्मादेवमानुषतिर्यक्प्रेतनारकाणां तत्तद्विशेषाणां च यथायथमेवानूकं पुरुषस्यान्वीक्षेत

hindi: वय तीन प्रकार का है: बाल, मध्य और वृद्ध।
english: Age (vayas) is threefold: young (bāla), middle (madhya) and old (vṛddha).
notes: Copula understood. 'bāla', 'madhya', 'vṛddha' are neuter adjectives standing for the age-stages (childhood, middle age, old age); the following units give the limits. 'madhyam' (not madhyamam) is as printed and is a regular neuter form.

hindi: इनमें सोलहवें वर्ष तक बाल है।
english: Of these, up to the sixteenth year is the young (age).
notes: Copula understood (verbless unit). Whether the sixteenth year is included is not stated ('ā' with the ablative is usually 'up to'); the translation keeps 'up to the sixteenth year'.

hindi: साठ तक मध्य; उसके बाद वृद्ध।
english: Up to sixty, the middle (age); after that, the old (age).
notes: Copula understood. The unit of count (years) is not repeated here; it is carried from the previous unit (varṣāt) and no word is added in the translation. Sandhi: ā+ṣaṣṭeḥ+madhyamam.

words.gloss: breast-milk; food; both; mode of living, subsistence

hindi: इनमें भी बाल अवस्था स्तन्य, आहार और दोनों की वृत्ति से तीन प्रकार की है। उसमें शरीर के परिमाण की वृद्धि और श्लेष्मा यानी कफ की अधिकता।
english: Among these also, the young (age) is threefold by mode of living: on breast-milk, on food, and on both. In it: growth in the size of the body, and predominance of śleṣman (phlegm, Kapha).
notes: [02.08.49] Copula understood. 'ubhaya' = 'both' (breast-milk and food together); the three kinds are not named in the text. Printed 'bālaṃtrividhaṃ' is a joining of two words only (bālam trividham). Dvandva read as stanya, āhāra, ubhaya. [02.08.50] Verbless; no verb added. 'tasmin' = in the young age. śleṣman (phlegm) is used here as the name of Kapha (standard).

words.gloss: unctuousness (sneha; or affection); softness; delicacy; little; anger; the state of; good fortune

hindi: इससे बाल अवस्था में स्नेह यानी चिकनापन, कोमलता, सुकुमारता, अल्प क्रोध और सौभाग्य होते हैं।
english: Because of that, in the young (age) there are unctuousness (sneha), softness, delicacy, little anger and good fortune (saubhāgya).
notes: 'sneha' is ambiguous: bodily unctuousness (taken here, as the effect of Kapha predominance in 50) or affection. 'saubhāgya' = good fortune (also charm, being loved). The compound ends 'alpa-krodha-tva' = 'smallness of anger'. Case of 'bālasya' read as 'in the young (age)' (genitive of the stage). bālasya is identical for masculine and neuter, so 'of the child' is an equally possible reading.

hindi: मध्य भी तीन प्रकार का है: यौवन, सम्पूर्णता और अपरिहानि।
english: The middle (age) also is threefold: youth (yauvana), fullness, and non-decline.
notes: Copula understood. The three stages are named only; their limits are given in 54. Spelling 'madhyamapi' = 'madhyam' + 'api' (regular writing of final m before a vowel), so there is no typo.

words.gloss: kindled; digestive fire (agni); the state of

hindi: उसमें पित्त की अधिकता; उससे अग्नि यानी पाचन-अग्नि की प्रदीप्त अवस्था, प्रज्ञा की अधिकता, परिपाक और व्यवसाय यानी दृढ़ निश्चय।
english: In it: predominance of Pitta; because of that, a kindled state of the digestive fire (agni), abundance of understanding (prajñā) and ripening, and determination (vyavasāya).
notes: Verbless; no verb added. 'prajñādhikyaparipākau' is dual: 'abundance of prajñā' and 'paripāka', read as 'abundance of understanding, and ripening (maturity)'; paripāka could also mean digestion, the sense is not fixed. The tā-compound dīptāgnitā means the state of having a kindled agni. The printed 'tenadīptāgnitā' joins two words.

words.gloss: all; dhātu; sense-organ (indriya); strength; vigour (vīrya); manliness (pauruṣa); memory; speech; knowledge (vijñāna); humility (praśraya); qualities; fullness; the state of

hindi: इनमें तीस तक यौवन; चालीस तक सभी धातु, इन्द्रिय, बल, वीर्य यानी शक्ति, पौरुष, स्मरण, वचन, विज्ञान और अनुमानित पाठ पर विनय के गुणों की पूर्णता; इसके बाद अपरिहानि।
english: Of these, up to thirty, youth; up to forty, fullness in the qualities of all the dhātus, the sense-organs, strength, vigour (vīrya), manliness (pauruṣa), memory, speech, knowledge (vijñāna) and, on a conjectural reading, humility (praśraya); after this, non-decline.

text_flags.why: possible: 'praśnaya' is not a word; 'praśraya' (humility, modesty) fits the list of qualities; n/r confusion

notes: Verbless; no verb added (copula understood). 'ā triṃśataḥ' = up to thirty, 'ā catvāriṃśataḥ' = up to forty. 'ataḥ param' = 'after this'; the end of the non-decline stage is given in 48 (sixty). The dvandva list read as the qualities of all dhātus, sense-organs, strength, vīrya, pauruṣa, smaraṇa, vacana, vijñāna, praśraya; 'vīrya' = vigour (not semen) beside bala; the exact scope of 'guṇa' is the commentator's. 'praśnaya' emended to 'praśraya' (flagged), so the last member is conjectural. Printed dhātviṃdriya = dhātu-indriya (regular sandhi).

wrinkle (valī); baldness (khalita; probable); cough (kāsa); breathlessness (śvāsa); digestive fire (agni); sinking, weakness (sāda); and so on

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √bhū (abhi), n. nom. sg.

hindi: वृद्ध अवस्था, परन्तु, दिन-प्रतिदिन धातु, इन्द्रिय आदि के गुणों के क्षीण होते जाने वाली, झुर्रियों, खलित यानी सम्भवतः गंजापन, खाँसी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, अग्नि यानी पाचन-अग्नि की मन्दता आदि से दबाई जाती हुई, वर्षा से भीगे पुराने घर की तरह बैठ जाती है।
english: The old (age), however, with the qualities of the dhātus, sense-organs and the rest wasting day after day, overcome by wrinkles, probably baldness (khalita), cough, breathlessness (śvāsa), weakness of the digestive fire (agni) and the like, sinks down like an old house rained upon.
notes: 'śvaḥ śvaḥ' (tomorrow, tomorrow) = day after day. 'jīrṇa' is read as 'old, decayed' (it qualifies bhavana), not 'digested'. 'khalita' = baldness (probable; the word can also mean stumbling). 'agnisāda' = sinking or weakness of the agni. The old age (vṛddham) is the subject of 'avasīdati'; 'jīrṇaṃ bhavanam iva abhivṛṣṭam' is the simile (neuter nominative). The case of 'abhibhūyamānam' and of 'kṣīyamāṇa...guṇam' (bahuvrīhi qualifying the age) is read from the form. Modern equivalents: valī = wrinkles, kāsa = cough, śvāsa = breathlessness (all standard).

words.gloss: loose; sapless, lacking essence; flesh; joints; bones; the state of
cough (kāsa); breathlessness (śvāsa); phlegm (śleṣman); nasal mucus (siṃghāṇaka); bringing up, expulsion

hindi: उसमें मारुत यानी वात की अधिकता; उससे मांस, सन्धियों और अस्थियों की शिथिलता और सारहीनता, त्वचा की रूखाई, शरीर का झुक जाना, कम्पन, खाँसी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, श्लेष्मा और सिंघाणक यानी नाक के मल का निकलना, और धातुओं का क्षय।
english: In it: predominance of māruta (wind; Vāta). Because of that: looseness and lack of essence in the flesh, joints and bones, roughness of the skin, stooping of the body, trembling, cough, breathlessness (śvāsa), the bringing up of phlegm (śleṣman) and nasal mucus (siṃghāṇaka), and wasting of the dhātus.
notes: Verbless; no verb added. 'māruta' = wind, a name of Vāta (standard). 'ślathāsāramāṃsasaṃdhyasthitā' is read as 'ślatha-asāra-māṃsa-sandhi-asthi-tā' (the state of the flesh, joints and bones being loose and sapless); the alternative parse '...sandhi-a-sthitā' (instability) is possible and the split is uncertain. 'siṃghāṇaka' = nasal mucus (standard). The compound 'kāsa-śvāsa-śleṣma-siṃghāṇaka-udīraṇa' may be read as cough and breathlessness together with the bringing up of phlegm and mucus; the translation keeps the list. Modern equivalents: vepathu = tremor; asāra = lacking essence (sāra).
lines_deva: तस्मिन्मारुतोद्रेकः तेन श्लथासारमांससंध्यस्थिता त्वक्पारुष्यमवनामः कायस्य वेपथुः कासश्वासश्लेष्मसिंघाणकोदीरणं धातुक्षयश्च
lines_iast: tasminmārutodrekaḥ tena ślathāsāramāṃsasaṃdhyasthitā tvakpāruṣyamavanāmaḥ kāyasya vepathuḥ kāsaśvāsaśleṣmasiṃghāṇakodīraṇaṃ dhātukṣayaśca

hindi: दूसरे लोग फिर कहते हैं:
english: Others, however, say:
notes: Introduces the view of 'others' stated in the next units (58-59); 'punar' = again/however. The next verse lines appear to be what they say.

words.gloss: lustre (prabhā); intelligence (medhā); skin (tvak); semen (śukra; standard); eye (akṣi); hearing (śruti); sense-organ (indriya)

hindi: बाल्यावस्था में वृद्धि; प्रभा, मेधा, त्वचा, शुक्र यानी वीर्य, आँख और श्रुति इन्द्रिय। दशकों में क्रम से मन और सभी इन्द्रियाँ जाती हैं।
english: In childhood, growth; lustre, intelligence, skin, semen (śukra), eye and the faculty of hearing. In the decades, in order, go the mind and all the sense-organs.

text_flags.why: possible, not adopted: as printed 'bālye vṛddhiḥ' is grammatical (in childhood, growth); but a list of ten items for 'daśakeṣu' (59) would need 'bālyam' as an item (childhood, growth, lustre, intelligence, skin, semen, eye, hearing, mind, all sense-organs)

notes: [02.08.58] GROUPING: 58 and 59 appear to be the two halves of one verse; the sense of the pair is not firm. The printed reading is kept (bālye, 'in childhood'). With the alternative 'bālyam vṛddhiḥ ...' the pair would list ten items (childhood, growth, lustre, intelligence, skin, semen, eye, hearing, mind, all sense-organs) against ten decades (daśakeṣu) of 59, which is a good argument for it, but the translation follows the print. 'śruti-indriya' = the faculty of hearing (śruti, hearing). 'prabhā' = lustre/radiance; 'medhā' = intelligence. Verbless; the verb is in 59 (yānti). Modern equivalent: śukra = semen (standard). [02.08.59] GROUPING: appears to complete 58 (the verb 'yānti' governs the items of 58 as well, on a possible reading), but this is not stated. 'yānti' = 'go'; whether it means 'depart/decline' or 'proceed/arrive' is not stated by the Sanskrit, so only 'go' is given. The verb is plural and 'manaḥ' singular (the plural verb also fits the list of 58). 'daśaka' = a group of ten (years), i.e. a decade; the word 'years' is not in the Sanskrit.

hindi: इस प्रकार सौ वर्ष आयु का प्रमाण है।
english: Thus a hundred years is the measure of life.
notes: Copula understood; 'is' supplied in the translation.

hindi: इस काल में किन्तु विशेष कर्म के कारण सौ वर्ष से अधिक न जीने वाले मनुष्य होते हैं। अनुमानित पाठ पर, उनकी आयु का प्रमाण कही गई प्रकृति की विशेषताओं से जानकर वय को तीन भागों में बाँटना चाहिए।
english: In this age, however, there are men who, because of a particular action (karma), live no more than a hundred years. On a conjectural reading, having ascertained the measure of their life by the particular marks of constitution (prakṛti) as stated, one should divide the age (vayas) into three.

text_flags.why: possible: 'viśaiśaiḥ' is not a word; 'viśeṣaiḥ' (particular marks, distinctions) gives the sense; ṣ/ś and e/ai confusion

possible: the print has 'anādhika' with a long ā, which is no word in this sense; read as 'anadhika' (not exceeding) in words, so this is an emendation (the opposite sense 'adhika', more than a hundred, cannot be excluded)

notes: 'an-adhika-varṣa-śata-jīvin' = 'living no more than a hundred years' (anadhika = not more). 'karma-viśeṣāt' = 'because of a particular (special) action' and may go with either 'santi' or the compound. 'asmin kāle' = in this time/age, not named further. The emendation to 'prakṛtiviśeṣaiḥ' is conjectural; the whole second sentence rests on it. 'yathoktaiḥ' = as stated (earlier). 'vayaḥ tridhā vibhajet' picks up 46-48. The form 'anadhika' in words is an emendation of the printed 'anādhika' (see text_flags); the sense 'no more than a hundred years' depends on it.
lines_deva: अस्मिन्काले संतिपुनः कर्मविशेषादनाधिकवर्षशतजीविनो मनुष्याः तेषां यथोक्तैः प्रकृतिविशैशैरायुषः प्रमाणमुपलभ्य वयस्त्रिधा विभजेत्
lines_iast: asminkāle saṃtipunaḥ karmaviśeṣādanādhikavarṣaśatajīvino manuṣyāḥ teṣāṃ yathoktaiḥ prakṛtiviśaiśairāyuṣaḥ pramāṇamupalabhya vayastridhā vibhajet

hindi: और भी।
english: And further.
notes: Formula 'api ca' introducing a further statement; the statement appears to be in the following units (63-64).

hindi: मनुष्यों के लिए, जब-जब सौ बीत जाते हैं, एक-एक वर्ष क्षय को प्राप्त होता है। आयु का, पुण्य की अधिकता के कारण, जो मान माना जाता है।
english: For men, each time a hundred has passed, a year goes to decay. Of life, owing to abundance of merit (puṇya), the measure that is accepted.

text_flags.why: possible: before 'p' the visarga would stay (āyuṣaḥ puṇya...); the line has 14 syllables where 16 are expected, so a word may have dropped out

notes: [02.08.63] GROUPING: 63 and 64 appear to be the two halves of one verse. 'varṣam varṣam' is read as nominative 'a year' with the singular verb 'yāti' and 'yāte śate śate' as a locative absolute 'hundred by hundred having passed'; the other reading is the adverbial 'year after year it goes to decay, as each hundred passes'. What decays (life, or the measure of life) is not stated here. The sentence appears to continue in 64. [02.08.64] The line is short by two syllables and is incomplete as a sentence (a relative 'yat' without its 'tat'), so a word may be lost; read literally. GROUPING: appears to continue 63. The measure referred to is of life (āyus). 'iṣyate' = is wished / accepted.
lines_deva: वर्षं वर्षं क्षयं याति नृणां याते शते शते
lines_iast: varṣaṃ varṣaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti nṛṇāṃ yāte śate śate

hindi: बल भी तीन प्रकार का होता है।
english: Strength (bala) also is threefold.
notes: The three kinds are named in 66.

hindi: सहज, काल से किया गया और युक्ति से किया गया।
english: Innate (sahaja), made by time (kāla), and made by method (yukti).
notes: Verbless list of the three kinds of strength named in 65. 'yukti' = application, contrivance, skilful method; kept as 'method' and explained in 69.

hindi: इनमें सहज देह और सत्त्व यानी मन का प्राकृत है। कालकृत ऋतुओं के विभाग से उत्पन्न और वय से किया गया है।
english: Of these, the innate (strength) is the natural (prākṛta) one of the body and of the mind (sattva). The time-made (strength) is born of the divisions of the seasons (ṛtu) and made by age.
notes: [02.08.67] Copula understood. 'prākṛta' = natural, belonging to the original constitution (prakṛti). 'sattva' = mind (standard). 'strength' is carried from 65 and shown in brackets in English only. [02.08.68] Copula understood. The two descriptions are read together as the kinds of time-made strength: 'born of the divisions of the seasons' and 'made by age'. Sandhi: kālakṛtam+ṛtu > kālakṛtamṛtu.

words.gloss: food; way of life (vihāra); arisen from

hindi: युक्ति से किया गया फिर आहार और विहार से उत्पन्न, ऊर्जा देने वाला और योग से उत्पन्न है।
english: The method-made (strength), again, is that arising from food and way of life (vihāra), the vigour-giving, and that born of yoga.

text_flags.why: possible: vowel length (u for ū in ūrjaskara); the missing space before 'yogajaṃ' is only a joining

notes: Copula understood. 'vihāra' = way of life, regimen of activity. 'ūrjaskara' = giving vigour. 'yoga' is ambiguous here (application of means, combination, or yoga); the kinds are read as three: from food and way of life, vigour-giving, and born of yoga. The sense of the last two is not firm.

hindi: परन्तु उसकी वृद्धि करने वाले ये भाव भी हैं।
english: But these conditions (bhāva), too, are producers of its increase.
notes: 'tad' = of it, i.e. of strength (bala). 'tu' = but and 'ca' = too are both kept; the second ca may also be 'and'. The conditions are listed in 72 (71 is 'tadyathā', namely).

hindi: वह इस प्रकार है:
english: Namely:
notes: Formula 'tad yathā' (that is, as follows) introducing the list in 72.

words.gloss: seed (bīja); field (kṣetra); qualities; body; food; sattva (mind); excellences

hindi: बलवान् पुरुषों वाले देश में जन्म और वैसे ही काल में; सुखद कालयोग; बीज यानी सम्भवतः वीर्य, क्षेत्र यानी सम्भवतः गर्भाशय के गुणों, शरीर, आहार और सत्त्व यानी मन की सम्पत्तियाँ; स्वभाव, यौवन, व्यायाम और हर्ष।
english: Birth in a region with strong men, and in a time of that kind; a pleasant conjunction of time (kāla-yoga); the excellences of the seed (bīja, probably semen) and field (kṣetra, probably the womb) with their qualities, of the body, of food and of the mind (sattva); natural disposition (svabhāva), youth, exercise and joy.
notes: Verbless list of the conditions that increase strength (70); no verb added. 'balavat-puruṣe deśe' = in a region with strong men (balavat taken as 'strong'). 'tadvidhe kāle' = in a time of that kind (the kind of time is not named). 'bīja' = probably semen/seed, 'kṣetra' = probably the womb (field), both probable. 'bīja-kṣetra-guṇa-...-sampatayaḥ' is plural, read as excellence of: (1) the qualities of seed and field, (2) body, (3) food, (4) sattva; the scope of 'guṇa' is uncertain. 'sukhaḥ' modifies kāla-yogaḥ. Printed 'sukhaśca' = sukhaḥ ca.
lines_deva: बलवत्पुरुषे देशे जन्म तद्विधे च काले सुखश्च कालयोगो बीजक्षेत्रगुणशरीराहारसत्त्वसंपतयः स्वभावो यौवनं व्यायामो हर्षश्च
lines_iast: balavatpuruṣe deśe janma tadvidhe ca kāle sukhaśca kālayogo bījakṣetraguṇaśarīrāhārasattvasaṃpatayaḥ svabhāvo yauvanaṃ vyāyāmo harṣaśca

words.gloss: skin; blood; flesh; fat; bone; marrow (majjā); semen (śukra); sattva (mind); consisting of
strength; measure; knowledge; for the purpose of

hindi: उसी प्रकार आठ सार यानी सर्वोत्तम तत्त्व बताए जाते हैं: त्वचा, रक्त, मांस, मेद यानी चर्बी, अस्थि, मज्जा, शुक्र यानी वीर्य और सत्त्व यानी मन स्वरूप वाले, जो अनुमानित पाठ पर उत्तरोत्तर श्रेष्ठ हैं, बल के प्रमाण को जानने के लिए।
english: Likewise, eight sāras (essences, best qualities) consisting of skin, blood, flesh, fat (medas), bone, marrow (majjā), semen (śukra) and mind (sattva), on a conjectural reading each better than the one before, are taught for knowing the measure of strength.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ātmakānyattara-' is not a word; the dropped vowel 'u' gives 'ātmakāny uttarottara-' (each better than the previous), which fits the rest

notes: The printed token joins many words with no spaces. 'sāra' = essence/best quality of a tissue; the eight sāras are skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen and sattva, each the 'consisting of' (ātmaka) item. 'uttarottaravara' = each next one better. 'upadiśyate' is singular beside the neuter plural 'sārāṇi' and is read impersonally 'is taught'. 'bala-māna-jñāna-artham' = for the knowledge of the measure of strength. The reading 'uttarottara' is conjectural (see text_flag); the translations mark it. Modern equivalents: medas = fat, majjā = marrow, śukra = semen (all standard).

hindi: और भी।
english: And further.
notes: Formula 'api ca' introducing a further statement, which begins in the next chunk.

words.gloss: body; only; from seeing: from merely seeing the body
large; body; -ness: from largeness of body

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वैद्य केवल देह को देखने मात्र से भ्रमित न हो कि 'यह उपचय यानी शरीर की पुष्टि से या बड़े शरीर के कारण बलवान है, और यह दुबलेपन से या छोटे शरीर के कारण अल्प बल वाला है।'
english: On a conjectural reading, a physician should not be deluded merely by seeing the body alone, thinking: 'This one is strong because of bulk (upacaya) or because of a large body; this one is of little strength because of thinness or because of a small body.'

text_flags.why: possible: 'mucyet' (should be released) gives no sense after 'na ... bhiṣak'; 'muhyet' (should be deluded) fits the quoted wrong inferences that follow; cy/hy confusion in the scan

notes: The printed 'mucyed' (mucyet, 'should be released') gives no sense here; 'muhyed' ('should be deluded', cy/hy confusion) fits the sense and is adopted on a conjectural reading, so the translations carry the mark. 'bhiṣag' is the subject; the two 'ayam' are the two cases quoted ('this one ... this one ...'). Printed 'balaiti' is 'bala iti' written together (hiatus). upacaya = accumulation, plumpness of flesh (standard).
lines_deva: न मुच्येद्देहमात्रदर्शनादेव भिषगयमुपचयेन महाशरीरत्वाद्वा बलवानयं कृशत्वादल्पशरीरत्वाद्वाऽल्पबलइति
lines_iast: na mucyeddehamātradarśanādeva bhiṣagayamupacayena mahāśarīratvādvā balavānayaṃ kṛśatvādalpaśarīratvādvā'lpabalaiti

words.gloss: elephant; lion: in the elephant and the lion

hindi: और वे दोनों भी हाथी और सिंह में अन्य प्रकार से देखे गए हैं।
english: And both of these are also seen to be otherwise in the elephant and the lion.
notes: Refers back to the two inferences quoted in 75 (strong from a large body; weak from a small body). 'gajasiṃhe' is read as a locative of the dvandva 'gaja-siṃha' (elephant and lion); the text does not say in which way each is 'otherwise'. 'api' is rendered 'also'.

words.gloss: supreme; heaviness, weight, gravity; joined with
with resonance; smooth; deep; great; voice

hindi: वहाँ सब सारों से युक्त होने वाला अत्यन्त बलवान, अत्यन्त गौरव यानी भारीपन से युक्त, क्लेश सहने में समर्थ, सब आरम्भों में अपने में आशा रखने वाला, कल्याण में लगनशील, स्थिर शरीर वाला, सुसंयत गति वाला, अनुनाद सहित स्निग्ध गम्भीर और महान् स्वर वाला, सुख, ऐश्वर्य और धन के उपभोग वाला, सम्मान पाने वाला, मन्द जरा और मन्द रोग वाला, प्रायः समान गुणों वाली विस्तृत सन्तान वाला और दीर्घायु होता है।
english: There, one endowed with all the essences (sāra) is exceedingly strong, endowed with great heaviness (gaurava), able to bear hardship, having hope in himself in all undertakings, devoted to the good, steady in body, of well-composed gait, with a resonant, smooth, deep and great voice, with the enjoyment of comfort, lordship and wealth, receiving honour, with slow old age and mild illness, usually with widely extended offspring of equal qualities, and long-lived.
notes: The sāras themselves are not listed in this unit; 'sāra' is rendered 'essence'. 'tatra' (there, among these) has no stated antecedent. 'gaurava' is bodily heaviness or gravity of bearing (dignity is an alternative sense). 'manda' is taken with both jarā and āmaya (slow/mild); 'prāyaḥ' (usually) could be taken with the preceding or the following phrase. 'vistīrṇa-apatya' = offspring that are extensive/numerous. 'sānunāda' = with resonance (anunāda). All adjectives qualify the one endowed with all sāras (subject understood from 'upaitaḥ').
lines_deva: तत्र सर्वैः सारैरुपैतोभवत्यतिबलः परमगौरवयुक्तः क्लेशक्षमःसर्वारंभेष्वात्मनि प्रत्याशावान् कल्याणाभिनिवेशी स्थिरशरीरः सुसमाहितगतिः सानुनादस्निग्धगंभीरमहास्वरः सुखैश्वर्यवित्तोपभोगः सन्मानभाङ्मंदजरामयःप्रायस्तुल्यगुणविस्तीर्णापत्यो दीर्घायुश्च
lines_iast: tatra sarvaiḥ sārairupaitobhavatyatibalaḥ paramagauravayuktaḥ kleśakṣamaḥsarvāraṃbheṣvātmani pratyāśāvān kalyāṇābhiniveśī sthiraśarīraḥ susamāhitagatiḥ sānunādasnigdhagaṃbhīramahāsvaraḥ sukhaiśvaryavittopabhogaḥ sanmānabhāṅmaṃdajarāmayaḥprāyastulyaguṇavistīrṇāpatyo dīrghāyuśca

hindi: उसका विपरीत तो असार यानी सार से रहित है; मध्य वाला मध्यम गुणों वाला है।
english: The opposite of that, however, is without essence (asāra); the middle one has middling qualities.
notes: 'tat' is taken as the one endowed with all sāras (77). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood). Whether 'asāra' means entirely lacking every sāra is not stated.

hindi: प्रमाण फिर अपने अंगुलों यानी अंगुल की चौड़ाई से है।
english: The measure, moreover, is by one's own aṅgulas (finger-breadths).
notes: Introduces the measurements that follow. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood).

words.gloss: of the foot; big toe; second toe (pradeśinī, lit. pointing one)

hindi: पैर के अँगूठे और प्रदेशिनी यानी अँगूठे के बाद की अंगुली दो अंगुल लम्बी हैं; अन्य तीन क्रम से आगे-आगे पाँचवें भाग से हीन हैं, या उनके नख से हीन हैं।
english: The big toe and the second toe (pradeśinī) of the foot are two aṅgulas long; the other three, in order, each successive one, are less by a fifth part, or less by their nail.
notes: Final -hīnā before 'vā' is regular sandhi (hīnāḥ vā). 'tat-nakha' = the nail of those (toes); the text does not say how a nail's length is fixed. pradeśinī (index finger) applied to the foot = second toe (standard). 'Other three' are the remaining toes, not named. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. Open: 'tat' in tannakha-hīnāḥ may mean the nail of the preceding toe or each toe's own nail; 'a fifth part' (of what) is also not stated.
lines_deva: पादांगुष्ठप्रदेशिन्यौ द्व्यंगुलायते तिस्रोऽन्याः क्रमेणोत्तरोत्तरं पंचमभागहीनास्तन्नखहीना वा
lines_iast: pādāṃguṣṭhapradeśinyau dvyaṃgulāyate tisro'nyāḥ krameṇottarottaraṃ paṃcamabhāgahīnāstannakhahīnā vā

words.gloss: front of the foot (prapada); sole (pādatala); heel (pāṣṇi)

hindi: प्रपद, पादतल और पाष्णि अलग-अलग चार अंगुल लम्बे हैं, और छः, पाँच और चार अंगुल चौड़े हैं; पैर लम्बाई में चौदह ही है और घेरे में चौदह ही है।
english: The prapada (front of the foot), the sole (pādatala) and the heel (pāṣṇi) are separately four aṅgulas long, and are spread six, five and four aṅgulas broad; the foot is exactly fourteen in length and exactly fourteen in girth.
notes: Pairing of the widths six, five, four with the three parts follows their order (natural reading, not stated). The three lengths of four plus the two of the big toe (80) make fourteen, which agrees with the foot's length; this is an observation only. 'aṅgula' is understood after the numerals. prapada = forepart of the foot, pāṣṇi = heel (standard). Final -āḥ/-aḥ before c is regular sandhi (vistṛtāś, pādaś). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: वैसे ही दोनों गुल्फ यानी टखने और जंघा यानी घुटने से टखने तक की टाँग का मध्य।
english: Likewise the two ankles (gulpha) and the middle of the shank (jaṅghā).
notes: Elliptical: no measure and no verb are printed here; both are carried from the neighbouring units, but the text does not say which measure. Unit 83 begins a new item (the foot's height). gulpha = ankle (standard); jaṅghā = the lower leg between knee and ankle (standard); in Hindi jaṅghā is not the thigh. Possible continuation of u81: 'tathā' may carry over a measure (e.g. girth) from the preceding unit, or a measure may have dropped out in print; not claimed.

hindi: पैर ऊँचाई में चार अंगुल का है।
english: The foot is four aṅgulas in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: जंघा यानी घुटने से टखने तक की टाँग और ऊरु यानी जाँघ लम्बाई में अठारह हैं।
english: The shank (jaṅghā) and the thigh (ūru) are eighteen in length.
notes: 'aṣṭādaśāyāmā' is feminine singular, agreeing with jaṅghā, and is understood for both. ūru = thigh (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: जानु यानी घुटना चार अंगुल का है।
english: The knee (jānu) is of four aṅgulas.
notes: The dimension (length, breadth) is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: ऊरु यानी जाँघ घेरे में तीस अंगुल की है।
english: The thigh is thirty aṅgulas in girth.
notes: Printed 'pariṇāhaūruḥ' = pariṇāhaḥ + ūruḥ (visarga lost in hiatus, regular). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न, दोनों लम्बाई में छः हैं और घेरे में आठ और पाँच हैं। कटी यानी कमर का भाग चौड़ाई में सोलह और घेरे में पचास है।
english: The muṣka (scrotum or testicles) and the meḍhra (penis) are both six in length, and eight and five in girth. The kaṭī (hip or waist region) is sixteen in breadth and fifty in girth.
notes: [02.08.87] Printed 'meṃḍhra' is read meḍhra (nasal before the conjunct; spelling normalised). Pairing 'eight and five' with the two organs in order is the natural reading, not stated. muṣka = testicle/scrotum (standard, the dictionaries give both), meḍhra = penis (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. [02.08.88] kaṭī = hip/waist region (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: bladder; head: head of the bladder

hindi: बस्तिशिर यानी मूत्राशय का शिर दस अंगुल का है।
english: The basti-śiras ('head of the bladder'; basti = bladder) is ten aṅgulas.
notes: basti = urinary bladder (standard); 'basti-śiras' is kept literal, and the exact part meant (the top of the bladder, or the region above it) is not stated here. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: उदर यानी पेट बारह अंगुल का है।
english: The belly (udara) is twelve aṅgulas.
notes: Here udara is the belly (body part), not a disease. The dimension is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: पार्श्व यानी पसलियों वाले दोनों भाग चौड़ाई में दस और लम्बाई में बारह हैं।
english: The two flanks (pārśva) are ten in breadth and twelve in length.
notes: 'vistāre' and 'āyāme' may be locatives ('in breadth', 'in length') or dual forms agreeing with 'pārśve'; the sense is the same. pārśva = flank, side of the trunk (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: trika (probably the sacral region of the lower back)

hindi: त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः पीठ के निचले भाग का त्रिकास्थि वाला स्थान ऊँचाई में बारह है।
english: The trika (probably the sacral region of the lower back) is twelve in height.
notes: trika = the lower back where the spine meets the pelvis, sacrum (probable). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: पृष्ठ यानी पीठ ऊँचाई में अठारह है।
english: The back (pṛṣṭha) is eighteen in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: स्तनान्तर यानी दोनों स्तनों के बीच का अन्तर बारह का है।
english: The interval between the breasts (stanāntara) is a set of twelve.
notes: 'dvādaśaka' = a group of twelve. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: स्तन का पर्यन्त यानी छोर दो अंगुल का है।
english: The limit (paryanta) of the breast is two aṅgulas.
notes: 'paryanta' = boundary, extremity; it may mean the breast's own extent or the edge region; the text does not say. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: उरस् यानी छाती चौबीस अंगुल चौड़ी और ऊँचाई में बारह है।
english: The chest (uras) is twenty-four aṅgulas broad and twelve in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: हृदय यानी दिल दो अंगुल का है।
english: The heart (hṛdaya) is of two aṅgulas.
notes: hṛdaya = heart (standard). The dimension is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of eight, a set of eight

hindi: दोनों स्कन्ध यानी कन्धे आठ के हैं, और दोनों कक्ष यानी काँख।
english: The two shoulders (skandha) are of eight, and the two armpits.
notes: 'aṣṭakau' is masculine dual and agrees only with 'skandhau'; that the armpits share the measure is understood from 'ca'. kakṣa = armpit (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of six, a set of six (conjectured; printed ṣaḍḍā)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, दोनों अंस यानी सम्भवतः कन्धे के जोड़ छः के हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading, the two aṃsa (probably the shoulder-joints) are of six.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṣaḍḍā' is not a form; the parallel dual numerals in 98, 100, 101 (aṣṭakau, ṣoḍaśakau, pañcadaśakau) suggest 'ṣaṭkau aṃsau' = ṣaṭkāv aṃsau (ṭk/ḍḍ confusion in the scan); conjectural

notes: Printed 'ṣaḍḍāvaṃsau' is not a regular form. The neighbouring units 98, 100, 101 use dual '-ka' forms (aṣṭakau, ṣoḍaśakau, pañcadaśakau); 'ṣaṭkau' + 'aṃsau' would give 'ṣaṭkāvaṃsau', close to the print, so this is a possible reading only. The numeral 'six' and 'aṃsa' are fairly sure; the middle syllables are not. aṃsa (shoulder or shoulder-joint) is probable; skandha in 98 is also rendered shoulder, and how the two differ is not stated here. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of sixteen, a set of sixteen
two prabāhu (an arm segment, identity disputed)

hindi: दोनों प्रबाहु यानी भुजा का एक भाग, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सोलह के हैं।
english: The two prabāhu (a segment of the arm; identity disputed) are of sixteen.
notes: prabāhu is given as 'forearm' in some dictionaries and as part of the upper limb in others; identity disputed, so the Sanskrit term is kept. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of fifteen, a set of fifteen
two prapāṇi (a part of the hand or arm, identity disputed)

hindi: दोनों प्रपाणि यानी हाथ या बाँह का एक भाग, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पन्द्रह के हैं।
english: The two prapāṇi (a part of the hand or arm; identity disputed) are of fifteen.
notes: prapāṇi is unclear: a length of fifteen is longer than the hand (twelve, 102), so a part of the arm is possible, but this is not certain; identity disputed, Sanskrit term kept. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: दोनों हाथ बारह अंगुल के हैं; उनमें भी मध्यमा अंगुली पाँच अंगुल की है। उससे आधा अंगुल हीन प्रदेशिनी यानी तर्जनी और अनामिका हैं।
english: The two hands (pāṇi) are twelve aṅgulas; in them as well, the middle finger is five aṅgulas. Less than that by half an aṅgula are the index finger (pradeśinī) and the ring finger (anāmikā).
notes: [02.08.102] Printed 'paṃcāṃgulāmadhyamāṃguliḥ' = pañcāṅgulā madhyamāṅguliḥ. 'tatra api' could also be 'even there (in each hand)'. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. [02.08.103] Printed 'arddha' = ardha (doubling after r, print habit; normalised). 'tataḥ' refers to the five aṅgulas of the middle finger (102). anāmikā ('nameless') = ring finger (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: कनिष्ठिका यानी छोटी अंगुली और अँगूठा साढ़े तीन अंगुल के हैं।
english: The little finger (kaniṣṭhikā) and the thumb (aṅguṣṭha) are three and a half aṅgulas.
notes: Printed 'sārddha' = sārdha (doubling after r; normalised). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: शिरोधरा यानी गर्दन ऊँचाई में चार और घेरे में बाईस है। आनन यानी चेहरा ऊँचाई में बारह और घेरे में चौबीस है।
english: The neck (śirodharā) is four in height and twenty-two in girth. The face (ānana) is twelve in height and twenty-four in girth.
notes: [02.08.105] śirodharā = neck (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. [02.08.106] ānana = face; āsya in 107 = mouth. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: आस्य यानी मुँह पाँच अंगुल का है।
english: The mouth (āsya) is of five aṅgulas.
notes: The dimension (opening, width) is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: chin; lip; nose; interval of the eyes; ear; forehead

hindi: चिबुक यानी ठुड्डी, ओष्ठ यानी होंठ, नासा यानी नाक, दृष्टि-अन्तर यानी सम्भवतः आँखों के बीच की दूरी, कर्ण यानी कान और ललाट यानी माथा, अलग-अलग चार अंगुल के हैं।
english: Separately, four aṅgulas: the chin (cibuka), the lip (oṣṭha), the nose (nāsā), the interval between the eyes (dṛṣṭy-antara, probably), the ear (karṇa) and the forehead (lalāṭa).

text_flags.why: possible: doubled d in 'nāsāddṛṣṭy-' is not required inside a compound; may be a spurious doubling, or nāsāt + dṛṣṭyantara (which would change the sense)

notes: Printed 'nāsāddṛṣṭy-' has a doubled d: either a spurious doubling (flagged) or 'nāsāt dṛṣṭy-antara'. 'dṛṣṭy-antara' is read as the interval between the eyes (probable); 'nāsā-dṛṣṭy-antara' as one item, the nose-to-eye interval, is a possible alternative. The compound is a neuter singular dvandva (caturaṅgulam). cibuka, oṣṭha, karṇa, lalāṭa are standard. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: a third part of an aṅgula in breadth
thumb; belly; spread: broad by the belly of the thumb

hindi: नासापुट यानी नथुने की मर्यादा यानी किनारा चौड़ाई में अंगुल का तिहाई भाग है। नेत्र यानी आँख दो अंगुल लम्बी है और अँगूठे के उदर यानी पेट की चौड़ाई वाली है।
english: The border (maryādā) of the nostril (nāsāpuṭa) is a third part of an aṅgula in breadth. The eye (netra) is two aṅgulas long and broad by the belly (udara) of the thumb.
notes: [02.08.109] 'tribhāga' is taken as a third part; 'three parts' of an aṅgula is an alternative. maryādā = border, limit. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. [02.08.110] 'aṅguṣṭhodara' = the belly, i.e. the fleshy middle of the thumb; the text gives no further measure, so it is not enriched. Here udara is a body part, not a disease. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: sight, the seeing part (probably the pupil)

hindi: उसमें कृष्ण यानी काला भाग शुक्ल यानी सफेद भाग का तीसरा अंश है; कृष्ण का नौवाँ अंश, मसूर के दल यानी मसूर की दाल की फाँक या पत्ते जितना, दृष्टि है, सम्भवतः पुतली।
english: In it, the black (part) is a third portion of the white; the dṛṣṭi (the seeing part, probably the pupil) is a ninth portion of the black, of the size of a masūra-dala (half of a lentil, or a lentil leaf).
notes: Read as 'the black is a third portion of the white' (śuklasya tṛtīyāṃśaḥ); 'tṛtīya-aṃśa' = one third or the third portion. 'dṛṣṭi' = the seeing part, probably the pupil. masūra = lentil, Lens culinaris (standard); 'dala' = half-seed, split, or leaf (ambiguous). Final -ā of 'navamāṃśā' agrees with feminine dṛṣṭi. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: छह अंगुल ऊँचा और बत्तीस घेरे वाला: शिर। फिर सारा शरीर चौरासी अंगुल है।
english: Six finger-breadths (aṅgula) in height and thirty-two in girth: the head. Again, the whole body is eighty-four finger-breadths (aṅgula).

text_flags.why: possible: printed as one word with the hiatus closed up; regular sandhi of śiraḥ + iti is 'śira iti' (spacing error)

notes: [02.08.112] Elliptical: no verb is stated, none is supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue from the previous unit (the subject of the measures is the head, śiras, named at the end). The closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement and is not translated. Orthography: anusvāra for a class nasal (ṣaḍaṃgula = ṣaḍaṅgula, daṃta = danta) is the print's habit and is normalised in `w` without a flag in this chunk; doubled rtt/rdd (varttā, varddhamāna) likewise normalised to rt/rd. aṅgula = finger-breadth, a unit of body measure. [02.08.113] Copula understood (none stated). The plural aṅgulāni and singular caturaśītiḥ do not agree in number; the sense is a measure equation. The count (84) is translated as printed.

hindi: उस लम्बाई और चौड़ाई में बराबर को सम यानी बराबर कहा जाता है।
english: What is equal in that length and breadth is called sama (even, symmetrical).
notes: tad is read as 'that (length and breadth)', i.e. the measure just given. The unstated noun (the body) is not supplied. 'sama' is given as 'even, symmetrical'; the text does not say more. Reviewer: alternative parse tad (separate pronoun, nom. n. sg.) + āyāma-vistāra-samam, i.e. 'that, equal in length and breadth, is called sama'; tadā ('then') is also possible. Open for the owner.

hindi: उनमें कहा गया परिमाण इष्ट है; कम या अधिक अनिष्ट है।
english: Therein, the measure as stated is desirable (iṣṭa); deficient or excessive is undesirable (aniṣṭa).
notes: Copula understood. The division of the clauses (iṣṭam | aniṣṭam hīnam adhikam vā) is the natural reading; hīnam/adhikam could also be read directly with the measure.

hindi: इस प्रकार, निश्चय ही:
english: Thus indeed:
notes: Formula 'tathā hi' introducing what follows (examples or a list); it is not said what follows.

hindi: इष्ट, फिर, बड़े सिर, दाँत, मुख, हनु यानी जबड़े, स्तनाग्र, पीठ और स्वर वाला; पुष्ट ऊरु यानी जाँघ, नितम्ब, कमर, छाती, गरदन और तालु वाला; दोनों गुणों वाले हाथ, पैर, ठोड़ी, कान और माथे वाला; सूक्ष्म हड्डी, दाँत, नाखून, उँगलियों के पर्व यानी जोड़ और केश वाला; लम्बी उँगलियों, सक्थि यानी जाँघ, भुजा, अनुमानित पाठ पर श्वास, दृष्टि, नेत्र और जीभ वाला; चौड़े मुख, निचले होंठ, जीभ, माथे, कर्णपीठ और छाती वाला, तथा छोटे मेढ्र यानी शिश्न, गरदन और केश वाला; चिकना, अस्पष्ट छपा त्वकचकरजन, नेत्र, दाँत और स्वर वाला; स्थिर इन्द्रिय, त्वचा, नाखून, केश और पार्श्व यानी पसलियों वाले भाग वाला; गहरी नाभि, जोड़ और स्वर वाला; छिपे हुए जत्रु यानी सम्भवतः हँसली का स्थान, पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ और दाँतों की जड़ वाला; लाल तालु, होंठ, नाखून और नेत्रों के कोनों वाला तथा हल्के लाल जीभ, हाथ और पैर के तलों वाला; काले केश, भौंह, नेत्र, पलकों और तारक यानी पुतली वाला, अस्पष्ट छपा शुक्लशुकमण्डलदशनचरित वाला, ऊँचे, छपे अनुसार चित्त, कन्धे, माथे, पेट, मुख, नाखून और पैर वाला; नीचे बँधे कान, स्तन, नासाग्र और चाल वाला; घने कन्धे और गरदन वाला, अस्पष्ट छपा वंतांगुलि वाला, त्वचा और सुहृद् भाव वाला।

notes: A very long run of bahuvrīhi adjectives (all nom./acc. sg.), joined in the print without spaces, in the style of a description of a desirable body. No noun is stated in this unit; the later units (to u136, where 'śarīram' stands) appear to continue the same description. GROUPING: appears to continue into u119 (same construction). Scope doubts: whether mahā 'large' applies to every member of its compound (head ... voice), whether upacita applies to all of 'thigh ... palate', whether dīrgha applies to every member of its compound, and what 'both qualities' (ubhaya-guṇa) refers to, are not settled by the Sanskrit; translated in the most literal way. 'stanāgra' = breast-tip (probable: nipple). 'karṇa-pīṭha' is literally ear-seat; the exact part is unclear. 'jatru' = collarbone region (probable). 'pṛṣṭha-vaṃśa' = spine (probable). 'meḍhra' = penis (standard). 'adhara-oṣṭha' taken as one item 'lower lip'; it could be two items (lower lip, lip). 'ātāmra' = reddish. 'netrānta' = corners/ends of the eyes. 'caṅkramaṇa' = walking, gait; 'nīcair baddha' = set low. 'citta' is printed 'mind' among body parts and is probably a misprint (not corrected). 'sauhārda' = friendliness, goodwill. Printed 'ucchāsa' conjecturally read as ucchvāsa (breath). Three stretches are unreadable and kept unsplit (tvakacakarajana; śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacarita; vaṃtāṃguli); translations leave them 'unclear' and give no meaning. Low confidence throughout. Reviewer conjecture, not applied: 'tvakacakarajana' + 'nayana' may be tvak-kaca-karaja-(na)-nayana, i.e. skin, hair, nails (karaja), eyes, within the snigdha series; one stray 'na'. hindi: अहंकार और दीनता के बिना सुख और दुःख को भोगता है। सत्त्वान्, परन्तु तप्यमान, राजस, किसी प्रकार भी अनुमानित पाठ पर तामस नहीं।
english: (One) experiences pleasure and pain without arrogance and without dejection. But sattvān, being heated (tapyamāna): rājasa, not at all tāmasa (on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: s/t confusion in the print; 'tāmataḥ' is not a word, tāmasa balances rājasa; the printed -ataḥ is not an ablative suffix here

notes: [02.08.142] The subject of sevate is not stated ('one'). anutseka and adainya are taken adverbially (neuter accusative) with the verb. utseka = arrogance, pride; dainya = dejection, wretchedness. It appears to continue u141; the text does not state this. [02.08.143] The sense of 'sattvān tapyamānaḥ' is uncertain: sattvān is a regular sandhi form (sattvān + tapyamānaḥ), accusative plural of sattva ('beings' or the quality), but it is not clear what it depends on (tap with an accusative is odd); tapyamāna may mean 'being tormented' or 'practising austerity'. The translation keeps the Sanskrit words and does not resolve them. 'tāmataḥ' is read as tāmasaḥ, hence the conjectural mark. The unit appears to be the second half of a sentence begun in u142 (not stated). Low confidence.

words.gloss: giving; conduct, character (śīla); compassion; truth (conjectural reading); continence (brahmacarya); gratitude

hindi: दान, शील, दया, अनुमानित पाठ पर सत्य, ब्रह्मचर्य और कृतज्ञता। रसायन यानी कायाकल्प के साधन, मैत्री, और पुण्य तथा आयु की वृद्धि के कारण वाला गुण।
english: Giving (dāna), conduct (śīla), compassion (dayā), truth (on a conjectural reading), continence (brahmacarya) and gratitude (kṛtajñatā). Rasāyanas (rejuvenation measures), friendliness (maitrī), and the quality (guṇa) that is the cause of increase of merit and life-span.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dayāstya' lacks the vowel after s (dayā-satya); 'astya' is not a word and 'satya' fits a list of virtues
possible: no space was printed between ca and puṇya (spacing error)

notes: [02.08.144] A list of qualities. Elliptical: no verb; it appears to be the subject of u145 (rasāyanāni …), but the text does not state this. brahmacarya = continence (celibacy); śīla = conduct, character. Reviewer: dayā-asteya (non-stealing) is an alternative to the conjectured dayā-satya for printed 'dayāstya'; not applied. [02.08.145] Elliptical: no verb. guṇaḥ is singular as printed (a plural guṇāḥ would suit the list better; not corrected). Whether this unit completes the list of u144 is not stated. rasāyana = rejuvenation measure; the text does not say what is meant here.

hindi: इस प्रकार प्रकृतिभेदीय नामक आठवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus the eighth chapter, named Prakṛtibhedīya (concerning the divisions of prakṛti).
notes: Colophon of the chapter. prakṛtibhedīya = 'concerning the divisions (bheda) of prakṛti (natural constitution)'.
